item.title: IndieWire and Lavazza Celebrated the Communal Experience of Cinema on the Independent Spirit Awards Blue Carpet
item.description: Our favorite filmmakers came together at the Hollywood Palladium to celebrate another year of independent film. Lavazza and IndieWire were there to capture it all.

item.title: ‘Industry’: Inside Eric’s Shocking Turn and What to Make of That Last Shot
item.description: Actor Ken Leung and creators Mickey Down and Konrad Kay take IndieWire behind the scenes of the conclusion of Eric Tao's Season 4 story, his Eminem-inspired TV debate, and if he'll be back.

item.title: The Independent Spirit Awards Winners Reflected a Scaled-Down Show
item.description: The Film Independent Spirit Awards swapped a massive beach tent for a concert hall and its big winners were more indie darlings than Oscar frontrunners.

item.title: ‘We Are All Strangers’ Review: Anthony Chen’s Immensely Entertaining Singaporean Family Drama Wears Its Heart Earnestly
item.description: Berlin: Multiple generations grapple with the onset of adulthood, and the crush of middle age, against a bustling Singapore backdrop in the "Ilo Ilo" and "Wet Season" director's emotionally generous fifth feature.

item.title: ‘At the Sea’ Review: Amy Adams Attempts to Float to Recovery, but Gets Marooned
item.description: Berlin: Kornél Mundruczó’s melodrama struggles to find perspective on Adams’ dance choreographer, who’s battling an alcoholism-driven midlife crisis.

item.title: Robert Duvall Dies at 95: An Actor Who Defined New Hollywood as Much as He Remained Unclassifiable
item.description: Across 60 years, from his debut as Boo Radley in "To Kill a Mockingbird" to his final role in 2022's "The Pale Blue Eye," the actor was associated with more masterpieces than possibly any other.

item.title: The Talented Mr. Whitney: Constructing the Con at the Heart of ‘Industry’
item.description: Creators Mickey Down and Konrad Kay take us behind the scenes of the glory hole, Whitney's letter, and why Episode 6 is the key to Season 4 taking flight.

item.title: Frederick Wiseman Dies at 96: The Documentary Legend Was One of Cinema’s Greatest Masters
item.description: Wiseman's 50-plus year career started with a bang with "Titicut Follies," and only got better.

item.title: ‘Isabel’ Review: A Brazilian Sommelier Dreams Small in a Film That Eventually Abandons Her
item.description: Berlin: Brazilian-American director Gabe Klinger loses interest in his attractive female protagonist

item.title: ‘Train Dreams’ Director Clint Bentley Recalls Support from His Crew During a Grueling Shoot: ‘Don’t Limit Yourself. Let Reality Limit You’
item.description: Bentley joined filmmaker and content creator Reagan Yorke for a Coffee Break with Lavazza and IndieWire at the Film Independent Spirit Awards.
